title: Report on the Execution of a Juvenile Offender in Dezful and Two Other Prisoners in Isfahan
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, two prisoners were executed on Wednesday morning, October 21, 2026, in Isfahan Central Prison.

The prisoners have been identified as Mobarak Mohammadi, 43, and Ghasem Molla Amini, 49, both Afghan nationals from the city of Sheberghan.

According to the report, the two prisoners had been sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court in a joint case involving drug-related charges. An informed source stated that they had been arrested approximately two years earlier on a road leading to Isfahan on charges of transporting drugs.

The source further stated that Mobarak Mohammadi was the father of four children, while Ghasem Molla Amini was the father of three. The two men were related and had been living with their families in the city of Mashhad.

Juvenile Offender Executed in Dezful

In a separate report, Iran Human Rights Organization stated that a juvenile offender was executed in Dezful Prison on August 19, 2026.

title: Three Citizens Arrested by IRGC Intelligence Agents in Asadabad
content:
According to HRANA, three citizens have been arrested in Asadabad. HRANA has verified the identities of the detainees as Javad Kouhi, Keyumars Heydari, and a citizen identified by the surname Rostami (first name unknown), all residents of Asadabad, located in Hamadan Province.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the three citizens were arrested at their residences by IRGC Intelligence agents on the evening of Sunday, November 1, 2026.

A source familiar with the case and close to the detainees’ families confirmed the arrests to HRANA, stating that the individuals face charges of “spreading false information” in connection with managing a Telegram channel and publishing content on it.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the detainees’ whereabouts.

title: January Protests: Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the death sentences of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi, two defendants in the case known as the “Ali Khani Square case” in Isfahan, were carried out this morning.

The Judiciary’s Media Center has claimed that four law enforcement officers were killed during the protests on January 8, 2026, in Ali Khani Square in Isfahan. The institution also alleged that a number of protesters attacked law enforcement officers and damaged public buildings and property.

In outlining the charges against Amirhossein Ebrahimi, Mizan claimed that he was present in Ali Khani Square on the day of the incident and, while carrying a bladed weapon, participated in the destruction of public property and the assault of law enforcement officers. According to the report, Mr. Ebrahimi went into hiding at a relative’s home following the incident and was subsequently arrested along with his brother.

title: January 2026 Protests: Alireza Dowlati and Mohammad Khalizadeh Sentenced to a Combined 35 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Alireza Dowlati and Mohammad Khalizadeh have been sentenced to prison. Based on information obtained by HRANA, Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced Mohammad Khalizadeh to 30 years in prison on charges of “moharebeh” (enmity against God) and Alireza Dowlati to five years in prison on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security.”

A source familiar with the case and close to the families of the two men confirmed the news to HRANA, stating that Dowlati and Khalizadeh are co-defendants in the same case as Omran Amani, a prisoner who has been sentenced to death.

The three men, who had been living together in the same house, were arrested in Tehran on February 11, 2026, in connection with the nationwide protests. All three are currently held in Greater Tehran Prison.

title: Two Women Sentenced to 22 Years in Prison Each in Connection with January Protests
content:
According to HRANA, two women have been sentenced to prison on charges of “espionage” in a case related to the nationwide protests of January 2026.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced each woman to 22 years in prison. HRANA has not yet been able to verify the identities of the two prisoners, and efforts to establish their identities are ongoing. Both women are currently serving their sentences in Qarchak Prison in Varamin.

A source familiar with the case told HRANA: “The two women initially faced the death penalty, but the judge ultimately granted leniency and sentenced each of them to 22 years in prison.”

The two women are co-defendants in the same case as three other individuals: Amirreza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and Mehdi Jalali, a cleric and former member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). All three men have been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

title: Three Detainees from January Protests Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, three citizens have been sentenced to death in Mashhad in connection with the January 2026 protests.

Based on information received by HRANA, the three individuals, one of whom has been identified as Matin Farnian, were sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, on charges of “moharebeh” (enmity against God).

The three were arrested by security forces in Mashhad on January 18 and 19, 2026, in connection with the nationwide protests. Following their arrests, they were transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, where they remain detained in different wards, including Ward 6/1.

Matin Farnian, 23, is a native and resident of Mashhad. HRANA is still working to verify the identities of the other two individuals sentenced to death in the same case.

HRANA’s investigation into further details of the case and the judicial proceedings remains ongoing.

title: Past Seven Months: At Least 118 Baha’i Citizens Subjected to Security and Judicial Measures in Iran
content:
According to HRANA, data collected during the first seven months of the Iranian year 1405 (March 21–October 22, 2026) indicates that these measures extended beyond arrests and prison sentences. In several cases, they also affected the family lives, property, economic activities, and access to education of Baha’i citizens. The highest numbers of identified individuals affected were recorded in Fars and Yazd provinces, with 25 each, followed by Mazandaran Province, with 23.

In this report, figures referring to individuals are based on identified Baha’i citizens, unless explicitly described as “cases” or “incidents.” A single individual may appear in more than one category, such as arrest, home search, or sentencing.

The security and judicial measures documented during this period affected Baha’i citizens across 11 provinces in Iran. Fars and Yazd recorded the highest numbers of identified individuals, with 25 each, followed by Mazandaran with 23.

title: January 2026 Protests: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence of Arman Marefati
content:
According to HRANA, the death sentence of Arman Marefati, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been upheld.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the Supreme Court upheld the death sentence of Arman Marefati, who is currently held in Ward 3, Hall 37 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. He had previously been sentenced to death by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, on charges including participation in operational activities against national security, entering religious premises with the intent to cause destruction, and involvement in setting fire to a mosque and a religious seminary.

It is worth noting that the death sentences of two other prisoners, Mehrdad Mohammadinia and Ashkan Maleki, who were co-defendants in the same case as Arman Marefati, were carried out in June 2026. The two prisoners had been sentenced to death on charges of “collaboration with the Zionist regime and hostile governments,” “creating insecurity and public fear,” “destruction and arson of public property,” and “participation in operational activities against national security.”

title: Mahshahr Writer Elias Ghanavati Lari Remains in Detention, Whereabouts Unknown
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Iranian Writers’ Association, Elias Ghanavati Lari, a writer and poet from Mahshahr, remains in detention.

According to the report, Mr. Ghanavati Lari was arrested by security forces on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.

Twelve days after his arrest, no information has been obtained regarding his condition or whereabouts.

His published works include the book Two Absurd Plays to Gather Dust and the article Proudhon and Marx at the Scene of the Theft.

title: One Prisoner Executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. HRANA has identified the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn on Sunday, November 1, as Iman Ashraf.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Mr. Ashraf had previously been arrested on a murder charge and subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.
